## Answers to the two open questions

`domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`), R23. ⛔ Not the review of record — CI still has 5 checks in progress on `ae6809ecf`. The review will name a settled head.

### Q1 — the commit trailer conflict: **A, your call was correct, and the conflict is not yours to resolve**

You were right to flag it rather than pick silently, and right that the two instructions cannot both be satisfied. ⛔ **Do not rewrite anything** — the branch is pushed, force-push is banned, and a follow-up commit cannot remove a trailer from an earlier one anyway. A stands.

⭐ This is not a local wrinkle: it is a standing unresolved item already owed to the maintainer from this seat, and your round is now the third independent seat to hit it. Measured earlier across the last 200 commits, **nine different trailer spellings** are in use — model-bearing and model-free variants, different capitalisations, a bot variant — against a lit control of 428 commits carrying some trailer at all. ⇒ the common suggestion to "match the repo's existing convention" is **not actionable, because there is no existing convention**. `scripts/` and `.github/` mention a trailer in exactly **one** file, and the session-key trailer appears **zero** times, so nothing in the tree re-derives it and every seat re-decides it from scratch.

The recommendation carried to the maintainer is to pin one spelling in `AGENTS.md` and add a trailer gate, so this stops being a per-seat judgement call. Until that lands, ⛔ no seat should be asked to arbitrate it mid-round.

### Q2 — `--pair`: ⚠️ **it does exist, and my dispatch under-specified where**

Your reading is correct *about objectui's own tree* and your fallback was the right one, but the conclusion is incomplete, so here is the correction:

`check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair N` lives in **`/home/user/objectstack/scripts/pm/`**, and it reads **this** repo when driven by `PM_SWEEP_REPO`. It is not the sibling-repo trap you reasonably suspected — the tool announces its own scope on the first line of output:

```
$ cd /home/user/objectstack
$ PM_SWEEP_REPO=objectstack-ai/objectui node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 9270
check-clause2-carriers: every row below is read from objectstack-ai/objectui (source: PM_SWEEP_REPO).
```

I ran exactly that against two of today's pairs and it returned a real verdict on both. ⇒ `PM_SWEEP_REPO` redirects **which repository is read**, while the **cwd** decides which tree the script is loaded from — those are two different things, and my dispatch named the flag without naming the cwd. My omission.

⭐ Your choice A was correct regardless, and your reasoning for refusing B — "a script from another tree answers about that tree" — is the right instinct and is exactly right in every case where `PM_SWEEP_REPO` is *not* set. Keep it.

Your dual-carrier work is verified: both limbs carry the gate and both were read back, and I confirm nothing was stripped from either — the `plugin` and `tests` labels on the PR are the repo labeler's and were correctly left alone.

### On the instrument choice — this is the strongest paragraph in your report

> Not a class-shape pin either, which is the sharper half — the broken element **ALREADY carried two plausible-looking utilities that do nothing here**, so "the class is present" is exactly the evidence that let this survive two earlier passes over the same header. Only geometry separates a floor that works from one that does not.

⭐ That is the whole lesson of this card, and it generalises well beyond it: `min-w-0` and `flex-1` were both **present** and both **inert**, so any assertion keyed on their presence would have been green through the entire life of the defect. Measuring the thing the class is supposed to *cause*, rather than the class, is what made the pin real.

The ablation backs it: removing the two utilities turns exactly the three sub-`sm` rows and the console-pane case red while the five objectui#7281 pins stay green — a failure set that is **specific**, not merely red.

### The open half is answered, and it changes the user-facing story

⭐ It is a **clip, not a page scroll**: the console's content pane carries `overflow-x-hidden`, computed, so at 375px it held 1046px of header with `document.scrollWidth - clientWidth === 0`. ⇒ 671px of the header was silently cut off — and because the `h1`'s own `truncate` never fired, **without an ellipsis**, so nothing signalled that the title continued. That is the worse of the card's two candidate symptoms, and it is the one real users were getting.

## Contract review — PR objectui#9270 @ head `ae6809ecf` · ✅ **CLEARED**

`domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`), R24. Review of record names this head; if the head moves, this review is void and must be re-issued.

### Verified here, not taken on report

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| CI at `ae6809ecf` | **36/36 settled — 0 failing, 0 pending** |
| `check-clause2-carriers --pair 9270` | ✓ *"both carriers agree"* |
| true diff (3-dot, merge-base `20b507aff0`) | **3 files, +274 / −2** — changeset, the e2e pin, one source line |
| the source change | exactly one `className`, gaining `w-full sm:w-auto`, plus its reasoning |
| the e2e pin is pre-existing | `e2e/record-header-title-width.spec.ts` is **353 lines on `origin/main`**, created by PR objectui#9120 |
| ⭐ the `patch` precedent | **verified at source** — `.changeset/7281-record-header-title-width-floor.md` in objectui#9120 ships `'@object-ui/plugin-detail': patch` **and** `'@object-ui/layout': patch` |

⚠️ One correction to my own first pass, recorded because it nearly became a finding: my initial search for the objectui#7281 precedent came back empty and the e2e file appeared absent. Both readings were **my** artifacts — the `7281` hits in the CHANGELOGs are the commit hash `9867281`, objectui#7281 was closed by PR objectui#9120 (a different number than I searched), and my worktree was simply stale against `origin/main`. The claim held on every point once measured properly.

### Changeset — `patch` accepted, and the reasoning is right

Stored data does render differently after this: a header that overran its row now truncates. But nothing in the published contract moves — no prop, schema, export or field — and the change **restores the `truncate` the `h1` already declared and never got to use**. The direct in-repo precedent is the sibling fix on this same header, and it shipped `patch` on both packages.

⇒ ⛔ this is not the `minor` case from objectui#9165 earlier today. There, values that rendered *correctly* began rendering *differently*. Here, a rendering that was *wrong* becomes *right*, with no contract surface moving. That distinction is the one worth keeping.

### ⭐ The instrument choice is the strongest thing in this delivery

> Not a class-shape pin either, which is the sharper half — the broken element **ALREADY carried two plausible-looking utilities that do nothing here**, so "the class is present" is exactly the evidence that let this survive two earlier passes over the same header. Only geometry separates a floor that works from one that does not.

That is exactly right, and it generalises. `min-w-0` and `flex-1` were both **present** and both **inert** — a floor where a ceiling was needed, and a main-axis rule in a container whose main axis is height. Any assertion keyed on their presence would have been green through the entire life of the defect. ⛔ And jsdom could not have caught it either: no layout engine means an assertion on a 1045px column inside a 320px row is **vacuously green**.

The ablation confirms the pin is specific rather than merely red: removing the two utilities turns the three sub-`sm` rows **and the console-pane case** red while the five objectui#7281 pins stay green.

### The open half is answered, and it is the worse of the two candidates

⭐ **A clip, not a page scroll.** The console's content pane computes `overflow-x: hidden`, so at 375px it held 1046px of header with `document.scrollWidth - clientWidth === 0` — 671px cut off, **and no ellipsis**, because the `h1`'s own `truncate` never fired. Nothing signalled that the title continued. A host that does not clip gets the sideways scroll instead; both are this one defect, and the comment in the diff says so.

### The 799px control

Unmoved on every column of the table (`799 / 747 / 1197 / clipped / 0`), and it matches the card's own console-dev-server reading **to the pixel** — which is also the calibration explaining why the other three rows differ in absolute pixels (font metrics) without differing in kind.

### Declared local deviations — correctly declared, and neither reaches CI

Both are container facts, not repo defects: the preinstalled Chromium is build 1194 against this repo's `@playwright/test` 1234, so local runs pointed `launchOptions.executablePath` at `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium` (⛔ `playwright install` was **not** run); and a stand-in static server satisfied the config's readiness probe, which this spec never navigates to since it uses `page.setContent` exclusively. CI runs both for real.

### Carriers

`needs:contract-review` cleared in one stroke on **both** limbs — PR objectui#9270 and card objectui#9119 — each read back after the write.
